title: Anaphylaxis: Recognition and Emergency Priorities
subject: Ward Protocols
preview: Anaphylaxis is a rapidly developing systemic hypersensitivity reaction involving airway, breathing or circulation; a rash may be absent.
quickRevision: Anaphylaxis is a rapidly developing systemic hypersensitivity reaction involving airway, breathing or circulation; a rash may be absent.
Airway swelling, wheeze, hypotension and collapse require prompt action and observation for recurrence.
Antihistamines can relieve some cutaneous symptoms but do not replace adrenaline for life-threatening reactions.

sections.title: Recognize the situation
points: Anaphylaxis is a rapidly developing systemic hypersensitivity reaction involving airway, breathing or circulation; a rash may be absent.
Intramuscular adrenaline in the mid-anterolateral thigh is first-line treatment alongside emergency support.

sections.title: Clinical decisions & differential
points: Airway swelling, wheeze, hypotension and collapse require prompt action and observation for recurrence.
Antihistamines can relieve some cutaneous symptoms but do not replace adrenaline for life-threatening reactions.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not delay adrenaline while waiting for a skin rash or laboratory test.

quiz.explanation: Intramuscular adrenaline in the mid-anterolateral thigh is first-line treatment alongside emergency support.
